findings.title: utm_data reaches the jsonb column as two different in-memory types on the two write paths (provably correct today; latent-fragility observation)
findings.description: The #create path builds expanded_params by ActionController::Parameters#merge (line 13), so the object passed to build_resource still responds to permitted?; ActiveModel::ForbiddenAttributesProtection#sanitize_for_mass_assignment (activemodel-6.1.7.7 forbidden_attributes_protection.rb:21-27) therefore calls expanded_params.to_h, whose recursive convert_parameters_to_hashes turns utm_data into an ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess before assignment. The #magic_create path (lines 88-115) builds user_params as a PLAIN Ruby Hash literal, so sanitize_for_mass_assignment takes the else branch (a plain Hash does not respond to permitted?) and NO to_h conversion happens; resource.utm_data is assigned the raw nested ActionController::Parameters returned by sign_up_params[:utm_data]. Both persist the correct jsonb payload: ActiveRecord::Type::Json#serialize (activerecord-6.1.7.7 type/json.rb:17) runs ActiveSupport::JSON.encode(value), and ActionController::Parameters delegates :as_json to its internal @parameters hash (actionpack-6.1.7.7 strong_parameters.rb:247), so a raw Parameters unwraps to the actual data ({"utm_medium":"cpc"}), not the {parameters:,permitted:} wrapper. The correctness of the magic_create path thus rides on the as_json delegation continuing to exist; if a future Rails upgrade dropped/changed that delegation, magic_create would silently store the wrapper object while #create (via to_h) would remain correct. No user-facing defect at this HEAD; noted so the divergence is on record.
findings.recommendation: Optional robustness only: build magic_create's user_params the same way #create does, or wrap the utm_data value so both paths hand ActiveRecord a plain hash (e.g. sign_up_params[:utm_data]&.to_h). Not required for correctness at Rails 6.1.7.7.

notes: Read the whole file (351 lines) plus the feature delta (git diff 62dd55867..fc3f047f9). Delta is exactly: sign_up_params permits :utm_source, :utm_campaign, :internal_ref, utm_data: {} (line 310, trailing hash-permit, matches the questions_controller.rb:50 options: {} analog verbatim); magic_create merges the four sign_up_params values into user_params in BOTH conditional branches (lines 97-100 connect branch, 110-113 default branch); #create threads them via the pre-existing expanded_params = sign_up_params.merge(...) -> build_resource mass-assignment (lines 13-20). CHECKS PERFORMED: (1) Mass-assignment safety -- all four are real users columns in db/schema.rb (users block: utm_source string, utm_campaign string, utm_data jsonb, internal_ref string); none is attr_readonly or otherwise protected; build_resource assigns them cleanly. (2) Key collisions -- both magic_create branch hashes have all-distinct keys (email, partner_source, created_via, password, password_confirmation, [connect_login_intent_organization_id], utm_source, utm_campaign, utm_data, internal_ref); no overlap with created_via/partner_source in #create's expanded_params either. (3) Guard ordering -- #create has no guards before build_resource; magic_create's only pre-merge guard is the Recaptcha::Verifier early-return (lines 75-79), which is UTM-agnostic; no guard rejects a utm-bearing request. (4) utm_data jsonb persistence -- traced serialize on BOTH paths (see F1); create-path .to_h -> HashWithIndifferentAccess and magic_create-path raw-Parameters -> as_json-delegated-to-@parameters both encode the same correct jsonb, verified against merge (new_instance_with_inherited_permitted_status keeps expanded_params permitted so .to_h does not raise UnfilteredParameters) and the as_json delegate at strong_parameters.rb:247. (5) Nil/absent handling -- sign_up_params[:key] is nil for an absent param on both paths; #create simply omits the key (column stays nil), magic_create explicitly assigns nil (column stays nil, jsonb serialize returns nil for nil so SQL NULL, not {}). No fabricated fallbacks (no || '' / || {}), matching D3/D6. (6) Existing-user branches -- the confirmed-user branch (lines 119-145) and the unconfirmed-resend branch (lines 146-157) read only user_params[:email] and never assign the utm attributes to the found User; only the else/new-user branch (lines 158-214) calls build_resource(user_params). Existing users are untouched, matching SPEC 4.2 / constraint 5. Structural comparison against the created_via/partner_source and questions_controller options: {} analogs holds. SETTLED RULINGS respected: did not re-flag M2 (connect-branch organization.id-on-nil crash + dormant merge keys) or M3 (bracket-key rack 400). Only new observation is the harmless two-type serialization divergence recorded as F1 (LOW).
